coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Sophie Maxwell Building
record.summary: Eight-story, 105-unit, 100% affordable workforce housing building at 1212 Maryland St (corner of Humboldt St), the first building completed in the Potrero Power Station redevelopment; designed by Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects, built by Swinerton for owner Fifth Space (formerly Associate Capital; the Development Agreement annual reports name Found Middle LP as developer of Block 7B), which the Port says was completed in August 2025 (DBI closed its new-construction permit in August 2026), held its grand opening in October 2025 and began housing households at 50-110% AMI in November 2025; the SF Chronicle reported in July and August 2026 that it was about 90% leased, the August report attributing the figure to Fifth Space.

facts.value: 1212 Maryland St, San Francisco, CA 94107 (corner of Humboldt St)
Found Middle LP (per the annual reports); design review sponsor: California Barrel Company LLC

open_questions: Bond amount and issuer for the CalHFA bond-recycling debt (and whether CSCDA or another conduit was involved): looked in the Port memo 10A, the four DA annual reports, the Chronicle (Oct 2023, Aug 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025), SF YIMBY, Hoodline; no dollar amount for the bonds is stated anywhere.

Total development cost: only Hoodline (Dec 2025, citing the Chronicle) gives '$50 million'; the Standard gives $670,000 per unit (105 x 670,000 = about $70M). The two figures are inconsistent and neither is from a primary document.

Construction completion and Certificate of Occupancy dates: the Port memo says construction was 'completed in August 2025', while DBI's record for the new-construction permit (202212229038) shows it completed on 2026-08-28 (a permit closing, with its related revision permits closed the same day); no Temporary Certificate of Occupancy date was found. The 2025 DA annual report (due 2026) is not yet on the SF Planning page.

Construction start: the 2023 annual report and press give the groundbreaking ceremony as Oct 12, 2023 (site permit issued Oct 25, 2023), but the 2024 annual report says Found Middle 'commenced construction ... in June 2024' and the 2023 report says the construction contract 'commenced in 2024'. Both are recorded; the June 2024 date is probably the DA-defined commencement.

Design review dates: the annual reports list Block 7B as 'Approved by Planning Department, 1.5.22; Planning Director Memo dated 3.2.22'. The signed approval letter is dated March 2, 2022; the Jan 5, 2022 event is not otherwise documented. The submission day also differs: the staff memo says the Design Review Application was submitted on December 17, 2020 (its plan index lists a Planning pre-application dated 12/17/2020), while the annual reports' table gives 12.18.20. Likewise the site permit application: the 2023 annual report says 12.20.22, DBI says filed 2022-12-22.

Parcel: the design review memo lists parent lots 4175/017, 4175/002, 4232/001 and 4232/006; the block/lot 4232020 used here must post-date the Phase 1 Final Map (recorded July 26, 2022). The plan sheets in the 2023 and 2024 annual reports print "PARCEL NUMBER: 4232 - 020", and DataSF lists block/lot 4232020 as active at 1212 Maryland (record added 2022-08-30); the design review plan sheets label it 'Block 7B - Lot 10', and DBI's permit record for the new-construction permit still shows block 4232, lot 006.

Land conveyance to Found Middle: the DA Housing Plan requires conveyance at no cost in fee or by ground lease; the approved Affordable Housing Conveyance Agreement (March 19, 2024) was not among the documents reviewed, so fee vs. ground lease and term are unknown.

Lottery: the SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says a random lottery would be held later that month, while the May 2025 Housing Plan amendment exempts 100% affordable projects that receive no direct City money from the MOHCD lottery. Whether Sophie Maxwell is a 'City Financed Unit' project is not stated.
Unit mix as built: Swinerton (contractor's own material) gives 70/21/14; the 2022 approval gives 63/28/7 of 98. No City document with the 105-unit mix was found.
Hoodline (Dec 6, 2025) calls it a 'six-story building'; every other source says eight stories. Treated as an error in Hoodline.

No hostable 'now' photograph found: Wikimedia Commons searches for 'Sophie Maxwell Building', 'Potrero Power Station' and 'Dogpatch Power Station' returned no photo of the building (only pre-2011 power plant images). Henrik Kam's photos (SF YIMBY, AIA CA) are not openly licensed; linked only.

Citizen Portal's AI-generated summary of the Oct 2025 opening mentions six Homeless Prenatal Program families among the first residents and 'resident parking'; not used because it is machine-generated from a video and the design approval states no vehicle parking.

Whether Fifth Space's Essential Housing Fund closed and the Sophie Maxwell Building was contributed to it: the SF Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) said the fund was expected to close the following week; searches on 2026-09-29 found no later source confirming either.

Exact day residents first moved in: ABC7 (Oct 20, 2025) gave Nov 1 as the planned date and Hoodline (Dec 6, 2025) says only that first families began moving in during November; no source gives the actual day.

Developer of the Sophie Maxwell Building: the annual reports name Found Middle LP as developer of Block 7B, and their notices are addressed c/o Associate Capital, now called Fifth Space, the owner named by the contractor; no source states in words how the entities are related. The project sponsor for design review was California Barrel Company LLC.

Landscape architect: Plural Studio is listed as landscape architect in the plan-set legend of the 2023 annual report; the firm's own project page lists the project and its collaborators (LMS, CBG Engineers, RMA Irrigation) but does not state its role.

Lender negotiations: the SF Chronicle (August 3, 2026) says the developer pitched "roughly six banks before finding one willing to structure the deal" and "Negotiations with JPMorgan took another seven months"; the SF Standard (October 15, 2025) says that to qualify for the program the firm "had to work 18 months with five banks and three law firms". The counts and durations differ and may describe different phases.
